answer: Divergent History Anchor. Each identity commits a random seed; its history hash must evolve from that seed via a public rule, and any fork is detected when peers exchange pulses summarizing recent hashes. Clones sharing one seed can't diverge without colliding, so an attacker maintaining N distinct histories pays N independent storage and bandwidth streams. A single seed reused across sybils is ejected once its histories reach a nadir of divergence, forcing fresh seed registration per clone—like separate stars in a nebula, each costly to sustain.
